# dsh-dump-manager

Sidebar entry, session table, the entry-stream viewer with two exports, plus the
newest-turn export

and its `LLM Dump` conversation tab, for dumps captured by
dsh-llm-dump.
## Install / remove
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The bundle has a host half (routes, exports) and a browser half (sidebar card,
panel, tab, settings

page). Host modules do not hot-reload: after editing one,
toggle the bundle so the Host re-imports t

t modules do not hot-reload: after editing one,
toggle the bundle so the Host re-imports the module.
## Levels
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Panel

- **LLM Dumps <size> · Exports <size>** beside Settings in the sidebar foot.
- Header repeats both s

izes plus session/request counts.
- Table: session/workspace, requests, size, last write, actions.
-

Row actions: view, folder (open the dump directory), delete (two-step).
- Session dumps live in `<o

utputDir>` (by default `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps`, one
directory per session); exports live beside it in

by default `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps`, one
directory per session); exports live beside it in `exports\`.
### Viewer

The viewer never shows request numbers as a dimension. It shows **entries** —
the typed units of the

er shows request numbers as a dimension. It shows **entries** —
the typed units of the conversation:
| type | meaning |

| `system` | the assembled system prompt |
| `tools` | the tool definitions block |
| `user` / `assi

stant` | conversation messages (tool calls included in assistant) |
| `tool` | a tool result message

ant` | conversation messages (tool calls included in assistant) |
| `tool` | a tool result message |

The last row may be the **tail entry** — the answer to the newest request, read
from `responses.json

l` rather than from a request snapshot. It is the only reply
that has not yet been resent as history

, and it carries a `最新回复` badge
(`最新·中断` when the stream was cut short).

- One continuous list per session. Each row: checkbox, type badge, one-line
summary, expand toggle.

- **缩略** renders the expanded entry as readable text (tool calls as
`→ name(args)`); **详细** renders

its complete JSON.
- Entries load 100 at a time: reaching the bottom loads the next page, and the
fo

oter reports `已渲染/总数`. `⤓ 到底部` renders every remaining entry of the
segment in one commit and jumps

to the end.
- The type row above the list selects or hides whole types: the checkbox
selects every e

ntry of that type in the current segment, clicking the name
hides or shows the type (hidden types st

ay selected; nothing is hidden by
default).
- A row's content is fetched only when it is expanded.
-

`全选本段` selects every entry of the current segment.
- `Shift+点击选区间`: a plain click on a checkbox set

s the anchor; Shift+clicking
a checkbox or a row adds the whole span between the anchor and that row

, in the
current visible order, so a hidden type is never swept in. Shift+clicking a
span that is al

ready fully selected removes it. The anchor stays at the last
plain click and resets when the segmen
t or the hidden types change.

**Segments (tabs).** The stream is one segment while each request only appends
messages. When a requ

est rewrites history (compaction, rebuild) the stream
breaks; each segment gets a tab. With a single
segment no tab bar is shown.
## Newest-turn export

`导出本轮 ▾` beside the session title exports the newest turn from the last
conversation request's snaps
hot (not from the entry stream):

- The turn starts at the last message whose `source.kind === 'user'`. Injected
user-role messages (`

time-context`, `runtime-context`, `agent-instructions`,
`skill-catalog`, `compact-checkpoint`, notic

es, `agent-message`, …) never
start a turn.
- The reply to that request comes from `responses.jsonl`

; it is not in any
snapshot yet.
- One-shot calls (session title, …) are skipped: a request with nei

ther an
assistant message nor a user message is not a conversation call.
Three persisted filters live in `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps\ui.json`:
| Option | Default | Effect |

| include user input | on | keep the `kind === 'user'` message |
| include tools | on | keep tool-ca

ll blocks and tool results |
| include injected context | off | keep the other user-role messages |

When the user's prompt was compacted away, the turn spans segments: each crossed
boundary must look

like a compaction (`messages[1].source.kind ===
'compact-checkpoint'`), retained messages are dedupl

icated, and the file carries
a note (Markdown) / `joinedCompaction: true` (JSON). Anything else is r

efused
with `409` and a code the UI turns into a dialog: `NO_DUMP`, `NO_USER`, `FORK`.
The dialog of
fers the viewer for manual segment export.
Files: `<title>_latest_<stamp>.md|.json` in the exports folder.
## Strings

All UI and export text comes from `lib/strings.js` (en + zh, English fallback).
The browser half can

not import it (plain script, no bundler), so
`tools/sync-strings.mjs` regenerates its inline copy an

d
`tools/check-strings.mjs` asserts the two copies and both languages agree.
## Export kinds

Both write into the exports folder (`<outputDir>\..\exports`), never overwrite
(`-1`, `-2`, …).
| Kind | Content | File |
| **transcript** | The selected entries only, rendered as Markdown, segments separated by `## 段 N ·

seq a–b`; a tail entry adds a note saying it came from the response stream | `.md` |
| **payload** |
For each segment represented in the selection, the complete request snapshot that last contained th
ose entries (`lastSeq`): unfolded messages + tools + tool history + sampling, one compact JSON line
| `.json`, one per segment |

Selecting every entry of a 132-request session produces a ~1.2 MB transcript
instead of the ~162 MB
the snapshot-per-request model produced.
## Settings page
`Settings → Plugins → LLM Dump Settings` owns two groups:

- **Newest-turn export** — the same three filters and format the header menu
writes, backed by `%DSH

_HOME%\llm-dumps\ui.json`.
[该节后续省略]
## Caveat

`payload` is semantically complete, not byte-identical to the wire body: the
folded store keeps valu

es, not the adapter's final serialization, so key order
can differ. Token counts match closely; exac
t wire capture needs a fetch hook.
